messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: stan::io::reader/writer Refactor Pattern
parts:
Right now the model has to do lots of validation,
making parameter manipulation a bit awkward. For
example, in model::transform_inits the model has
to construct an io::writer with internal storage for
unconstrained parameters, then one by one check
that a variable exists in the var_context, grab
it, validate its dimensions, and then finally
map it to the unconstrained scale and append the
unconstrained values into the io::writer’s internal
storage before copying into the model storage:

void model::transform_inits(…) {

stan::io::writer<double> writer__(params_r__,params_i__);
size_t pos__;
std::vector<double> vals_r__;
…

if (!(context__.contains_r("mu1")))
throw std::runtime_error("variable mu1 missing");
vals_r__ = context__.vals_r("mu1");
pos__ = 0U;
context__.validate_dims("initialization", "mu1", "double", context__.to_vec());
double mu1(0);
mu1 = vals_r__[pos__++];
try {
writer__.scalar_lb_unconstrain(0, mu1);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
throw std::runtime_error(std::string("Error transforming variable mu1: ") + e.what());
}
…
params_r__ = writer__.data_r();
}

using the var_context methods

bool var_context::contains_r(const std::string& param_name);
std::vector<double> var_context::vals_r(const std::string& name);
void var_context::validate_dims(const std::string& stage,
const std::string& name,
const std::string& base_type,
const std::vector<size_t>& dims_declared);

This is not only extra work for the parser, it makes
implementing features like partial random inits a bit kludgy.

In order to clean up the interaction of the API with
both constrain/unconstrain transformations and the
var_context (making it easier to access the transformations
directly and pull the var_contexts out into the interfaces)
I am proposing the following changes.

First, io::writer and io::reader will be replaced with
a set of functors responsible for a given transformation,

class transform {
static virtual void constrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
std::vector<double>& output) = 0;
static virtual void unconstrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
std::vector<double>& output) = 0;
static int constrained_dim();
static int unconstrained_dim();
static std::string base_type();
}

For example, a lower bound constraint would be
handled by the functor

<double LowerBound>
class lb_transform: public transform {
static void constrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
std::vector<double>& output) {
output.push_back(stan::prob::lb_constrain(input, LowerBound));
}
static void unconstrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
std::vector<double>& output) {
output.push_back(stan::prob::lb_free(input, LowerBound));
}
static int constrained_dim() { return 1; }
static int unconstrained_dim() { return 1; }
static std::string base_type() { return “double”; }
}

and the io::writer::scalar_lb_unconstrain(0, mu1) call
in model::transform_inits could be immediately replaced by
lb_transform<0>::unconstrain(mu1, params_r_).

With these functors available we can now move all of the
validation into the var_context,

template <Transform>
void var_context::get_unconstrained(const vector<double>& params_r,
const string& stage,
const string& param_name,
int constrained_dim) {
if (!(this->contains_r(param_name)))
throw std::runtime_error("variable “ + param_name + “ missing");
validate_dims(stage, param_name, Transform::base_type(), constrained_dim))

params_r.append(Transform::unconstrain(vars_r(param_name)));
}

and then the model becomes simply

void model::transform_inits(…) {

params_r.clear();
…
try {
context__.get_unconstrained<lb_transform<0> >(params_r,
“initialization”,
“mu1”, 1);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
throw std::runtime_error(std::string("Error initializing variable mu1: ") + e.what());
}
}

Moreover, partial random inits become as simple as

<template VarContext>
class random_fallback_var_context {

template <Transform>
void var_context::get_unconstrained(const vector<double>& params_r,
const string& stage,
const string& param_name,
int constrained_dim) {

if ( !(base_context.contains_r(param_name)))
&& !(validate_dims(stage, param_name, Transform::base_type(), constrained_dim)))
params_r.append(Transform::unconstrain(base_context.vars_r(param_name)));
else
params_r.append(random_array(Transform::unconstrained_dim()));
}

VarContext& base_context;

}

Of course there are lots of subtleties that will have to
be fixed along the way, but what do people think of the
basic pattern?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan::io::reader/writer Refactor Pattern
parts:
I'm totally on board with this kind of clean up in
the code generator and reader/writer interfaces. (It's
not actually a problem with the parser, per se.)

Let's do it right this time. Some detailed comments inline.

> On Apr 4, 2015, at 2:15 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Right now the model has to do lots of validation,
> making parameter manipulation a bit awkward.
It's more than a bit awkward --- it's a mess!

> For
> example, in model::transform_inits the model has
> to construct an io::writer with internal storage for
> unconstrained parameters,

Recall that transform_inits takes variables declared
on the constrained scale (through a var_context) to a vector of
unconstrained variables.

So somewhere there has to be memory for the unconstrained
variables.

> then one by one check
> that a variable exists in the var_context, grab
> it, validate its dimensions, and then finally
> map it to the unconstrained scale and append the
> unconstrained values into the io::writer’s internal
> storage before copying into the model storage:
>

Here's the full signature:

void transform_inits(const stan::io::var_context& context__,
std::vector<int>& params_i__,
std::vector<double>& params_r__,
std::ostream* pstream__) const {


We need to get rid of those "__" at some point --- they're there
to avoid name conflicts with user-defined variables, but some
other mangling is in order.

> void model::transform_inits(…) {
>
> stan::io::writer<double> writer__(params_r__,params_i__);
> size_t pos__;
> std::vector<double> vals_r__;
> …
>
> if (!(context__.contains_r("mu1")))
> throw std::runtime_error("variable mu1 missing");
This shold be an error thrown by the context itself.

> vals_r__ = context__.vals_r("mu1");
> pos__ = 0U;
> context__.validate_dims("initialization", "mu1", "double", context__.to_vec());
This validation should also be done by the context itself.

> double mu1(0);
> mu1 = vals_r__[pos__++];
> try {
> writer__.scalar_lb_unconstrain(0, mu1);
> } catch (const std::exception& e) {
> throw std::runtime_error(std::string("Error transforming variable mu1: ") + e.what());
> }

This transform is already done in the writer. What I'd suggest
is passing in the name "mu1" to the unconstrain function.

We also want to specialize the lb (lower bound) unconstrain so
that 0 doesn't show up. That is, we want a test for zero somewhere
and then just a straight log transform.

> …
> params_r__ = writer__.data_r();
> }
>
> using the var_context methods
>
> bool var_context::contains_r(const std::string& param_name);
> std::vector<double> var_context::vals_r(const std::string& name);
> void var_context::validate_dims(const std::string& stage,
> const std::string& name,
> const std::string& base_type,
> const std::vector<size_t>& dims_declared);
>
> This is not only extra work for the parser, it makes
> implementing features like partial random inits a bit kludgy.
Absolutely. And again, I'd say it's more than a bit kludgy!

> In order to clean up the interaction of the API with
> both constrain/unconstrain transformations and the
> var_context (making it easier to access the transformations
> directly and pull the var_contexts out into the interfaces)
> I am proposing the following changes.
>
> First, io::writer and io::reader will be replaced with
> a set of functors responsible for a given transformation,

A functor defines operator() --- these are are just classes
with member functions.

> class transform {
> static virtual void constrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
> std::vector<double>& output) = 0;
> static virtual void unconstrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
> std::vector<double>& output) = 0;
> static int constrained_dim();
> static int unconstrained_dim();
> static std::string base_type();
> }

The base_type should be a typedef, not a string. Or if it
needs a string, then the method should be called "base_type_name()".

> For example, a lower bound constraint would be
> handled by the functor
>
> <double LowerBound>
> class lb_transform: public transform {
> static void constrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
> std::vector<double>& output) {
> output.push_back(stan::prob::lb_constrain(input, LowerBound));
> }
> static void unconstrain(const std::vector<double>& input,
> std::vector<double>& output) {
> output.push_back(stan::prob::lb_free(input, LowerBound));
> }
> static int constrained_dim() { return 1; }
> static int unconstrained_dim() { return 1; }
> static std::string base_type() { return “double”; }
> }

This isn't quite C++ --- you can't have virtual static functions
because there's no object to dynamically resolve the function definition.
But it can all be concept driven with no abstract base
class. Or it could use the CRTP to get the performance of a static
and some of the benefits of an abstract base class in terms of
more transparent specs.

> and the io::writer::scalar_lb_unconstrain(0, mu1) call
> in model::transform_inits could be immediately replaced by
> lb_transform<0>::unconstrain(mu1, params_r_).

Yes, and maybe we could add "mu1" as an argument so we can
do the error checking?

> With these functors available we can now move all of the
> validation into the var_context,
>
> template <Transform>
> void var_context::get_unconstrained(const vector<double>& params_r,
> const string& stage,
> const string& param_name,
> int constrained_dim) {
> if (!(this->contains_r(param_name)))
> throw std::runtime_error("variable “ + param_name + “ missing");
> validate_dims(stage, param_name, Transform::base_type(), constrained_dim))
>
> params_r.append(Transform::unconstrain(vars_r(param_name)));
> }
Agreed --- that's where it belongs.

> and then the model becomes simply
>
> void model::transform_inits(…) {
>
> params_r.clear();
> …
> try {
> context__.get_unconstrained<lb_transform<0> >(params_r,
> “initialization”,
> “mu1”, 1);
> } catch (const std::exception& e) {
> throw std::runtime_error(std::string("Error initializing variable mu1: ") + e.what());
> }
> }

None of those curly quotes, though! :-)

And given that we're passing "mu1" in, we can also have the
exception be thrown from the var_context itself.

I'm wondering if that'll be redundant for the different interfaces.
There's got to be a way to keep it defined only once and not in
the generated model code as it's done now, which is more than a bit
awkward.

> Moreover, partial random inits become as simple as
>
> <template VarContext>
> class random_fallback_var_context {
>
> template <Transform>
> void var_context::get_unconstrained(const vector<double>& params_r,
> const string& stage,
> const string& param_name,
> int constrained_dim) {
>
> if ( !(base_context.contains_r(param_name)))
> && !(validate_dims(stage, param_name, Transform::base_type(), constrained_dim)))
> params_r.append(Transform::unconstrain(base_context.vars_r(param_name)));
> else
> params_r.append(random_array(Transform::unconstrained_dim()));
> }
>
> VarContext& base_context;
>
> }
>
Nice.

> Of course there are lots of subtleties that will have to
> be fixed along the way, but what do people think of the
> basic pattern?

Great idea. We should've done this ages ago.

- Bob
